# Settings

203 settings, by section (the Settings page's tabs) then name. Change one with `:set NAME=VALUE`, `settings set NAME VALUE` or the Settings page; the values live in settings.json.

## About

<a id="setting-about.dep-prefixes"></a>
### `about.dep-prefixes`

list · default `["ofam.dev/","github.com/ofamtools/","github.com/unixsuperhero/"]` · section About · declared by ochazuke

Module path prefixes whose modules the About page's Dependencies section lists, with their versions and where a replace or a go.work points them; empty lists none

<a id="setting-about.tab"></a>
### `about.tab`

boolean · default `true` · section About · declared by ochazuke

Show the About page as a tab of the Settings page: ] and [ step from the last tab to About and back, and the About page draws the Settings page's tabs; off, about.open still opens the page on its own

## Agents

<a id="setting-agents.confirm-attribution"></a>
### `agents.confirm-attribution`

boolean · default `true` · section Agents · declared by ochazuke

Name the agent asking in confirmation prompts

<a id="setting-agents.rights"></a>
### `agents.rights`

string · default `[]` · section Agents · declared by ochazuke

Ordered JSON rows {match, right, where}: noun.verb, noun.* or *; allow, confirm or never; any, live or headless

<a id="setting-agents.rights-gate"></a>
### `agents.rights-gate`

boolean · default `true` · section Agents · declared by ochazuke

Enforce agent rights on every request; off gives agents owner rights

<a id="setting-agents.status-segment"></a>
### `agents.status-segment`

boolean · default `false` · section Agents · declared by ochazuke

Show the agent with an active job or a pending confirmation in the header status segments

<a id="setting-mcp.include-extensions"></a>
### `mcp.include-extensions`

boolean · default `false` · section Agents · declared by ochazuke

Include mounted extension verbs in this app MCP catalog; off, use each extension own server

<a id="setting-mcp.instructions-nouns"></a>
### `mcp.instructions-nouns`

string · default `all` · choices `all`, `names`, `first` · section Agents · declared by ochazuke

Nouns and extensions in MCP startup instructions: all lists every one (name, verb count, short description; names only when text would pass the cap); names lists names only on a wrapped paragraph; first lists a few and ends with N more: call catalog

## Appearance

<a id="setting-chrome.border"></a>
### `chrome.border`

string · default `rounded` · choices `rounded`, `square`, `classic` · section Appearance · declared by ochazuke

Border shapes for panels, modals, completions and cards: rounded has joined heavy focused corners, square has square light corners, classic restores the original mixed-weight focused panel corners. All keep the same cell sizes

<a id="setting-chrome.color"></a>
### `chrome.color`

string · default `rich` · choices `off`, `subtle`, `rich` · section Appearance · declared by ochazuke

Colour in the chrome: rich colours borders by state or mode, fills the badge and active tab, draws quiet border-coloured rules, colours job entries and gives errors a background; subtle tints the badge and active tab, alert borders and job state words; off restores the original chrome. themes.json tones named chrome.<level>.<role> change any of it

<a id="setting-chrome.glyphs"></a>
### `chrome.glyphs`

string · default `auto` · choices `auto`, `ascii`, `unicode`, `nerd` · section Appearance · declared by ochazuke

Chrome marks: auto uses ASCII only on a real non-UTF-8 terminal or TERM=linux, otherwise today's Unicode; ascii converts the whole TUI frame to 7-bit at the same cell widths; unicode keeps today's marks; nerd opts into Nerd Font Mono icons. glyphs list explains auto; glyphs show previews the roles

<a id="setting-collection.cell-cursor"></a>
### `collection.cell-cursor`

string · default `background` · choices `background`, `underline` · section Appearance · declared by ochazuke

A cell-mode table's current cell on the selected row: background draws it in the list.cell.cursor tone (the scheme's surface on its accent, bold), out of the reverse bar; underline draws it reversed and underlined inside the bar, as before

<a id="setting-collection.intersect"></a>
### `collection.intersect`

boolean · default `true` · section Appearance · declared by ochazuke

Where two highlights cross in a table (the selected row and a highlighted column, a highlighted row and column, a search hit on the selected row), the cell takes its part's intersect tone (list.cell.intersect, list.header.intersect, list.rownum.intersect) so the crossing reads at a glance; off draws the highlights as before, the later one winning

<a id="setting-collection.part-tones"></a>
### `collection.part-tones`

boolean · default `true` · section Appearance · declared by ochazuke

A table's header row and its non-data columns (row numbers) draw in their own tones (list.header, list.rownum) so they never read as data; off draws the header bold and those columns as data, as before

<a id="setting-dim-unfocused"></a>
### `dim-unfocused`

integer · default `20` · section Appearance · declared by ochazuke

Percent a list without the focus fades toward the background; its selected row stays marked (0 is off)

<a id="setting-dim-unfocused-selection"></a>
### `dim-unfocused-selection`

integer · default `30` · section Appearance · declared by ochazuke

Percent the selected row's bar in a list without the focus fades toward the background beyond dim-unfocused, so the focused list's bar is the bright one; the row stays marked (0 fades it with the list; mono and NO_COLOR keep the faint bar)

<a id="setting-focus-display"></a>
### `focus-display`

string · default `off` · choices `off`, `noun`, `stack` · section Appearance · declared by ochazuke

Show where the focus is, left of the mode badge: off, noun (the focused noun) or stack (the focus path, outermost first)

<a id="setting-modal-dim"></a>
### `modal-dim`

integer · default `35` · section Appearance · declared by ochazuke

Percent the page behind a modal fades toward the background (0 is off)

<a id="setting-modal-highlights"></a>
### `modal-highlights`

string · default `keep` · choices `keep`, `plain` · section Appearance · declared by ochazuke

The page's highlights beneath a modal: keep draws them dimmed (a list's cursor bar, a grid's cursor cell, so you see where you were); plain draws the backdrop without reverse video or underline, so no sliver of a cursor bar shows beside a wide modal

<a id="setting-modal.anchor"></a>
### `modal.anchor`

boolean · default `true` · section Appearance · declared by ochazuke

A modal opened for something on the page (a form field's picker) is drawn beside it, sized to its rows, so the field and the lines around it stay visible (below or above it when there is no room beside); off centers it as every other modal

<a id="setting-mode-badge.key-case"></a>
### `mode-badge.key-case`

string · default `upper` · choices `upper`, `as-typed` · section Appearance · declared by ochazuke

The keys a pending mode holds in the mode badge: upper (NORMAL G for both g and G, LEADER PENDING CTRL+A) or as-typed (NORMAL g, NORMAL G, LEADER PENDING ctrl+a); the mode's name stays upper case

<a id="setting-mode-badge.width"></a>
### `mode-badge.width`

string · default `widest` · choices `widest`, `fit` · section Appearance · declared by ochazuke

The cells the mode badge takes at the right end of the title row: widest pads every mode to the widest mode's name, so the badge holds still as the mode changes; fit draws each mode in its own cells (only its right edge holds still)

<a id="setting-render.max-fps"></a>
### `render.max-fps`

integer · default `30` · section Appearance · declared by ochazuke

Maximum background frame compositions per second; 0 disables frame reuse and coalescing; keys and resize draw immediately

<a id="setting-theme"></a>
### `theme`

string · default `adaptive` · choices `adaptive`, `dark`, `light`, `mono` · section Appearance · declared by ochazuke

Colour scheme (themes.json adds more)

<a id="setting-tones.selected-background"></a>
### `tones.selected-background`

string · default `drop` · choices `drop`, `keep` · section Appearance · declared by ochazuke

A cell drawn on a tone background (an error) on the selected row: drop keeps the row one reverse bar; keep draws the cell on its background, bold, out of the bar

<a id="setting-unfocused-selection"></a>
### `unfocused-selection`

string · default `keep` · choices `keep`, `hide` · section Appearance · declared by ochazuke

A list, table, grid, Doc, settings selector or app row without the focus: keep draws its selection marked and faded (dim-unfocused, dim-unfocused-selection), so you see where each one is; hide draws only the focused component's selection

## Help

<a id="setting-docs.show-config"></a>
### `docs.show-config`

boolean · default `true` · section Help · declared by ochazuke

The docs viewer (docs open, :help) marks where your settings.json and bindings.json differ from the defaults with yours: lines; off, a page reads as the committed reference

<a id="setting-help.description-max"></a>
### `help.description-max`

integer · default `80` · section Help · declared by ochazuke

The ? help's description column wraps within this many cells, leaving the room to the other columns; 0 lets it take all the width left

<a id="setting-help.hints-hidden"></a>
### `help.hints-hidden`

boolean · default `false` · section Help · declared by ochazuke

The footer and every modal's hint line also show the rows marked hidden: the editor's insert keys (ctrl+k, ctrl+w, backspace), the palette key ctrl+space, counts and registers; off leaves them to ? help and bindings list, as motions are

<a id="setting-help.markdown"></a>
### `help.markdown`

boolean · default `true` · section Help · declared by ochazuke

Help and docs text in a modal (the docs viewer, :help, a verb's Markdown or preformatted answer such as a command's --help) opens in the Markdown viewer: headings, code, wrapping, link stops, j/k by element, q or esc to close, y a to copy it all; off shows it as plain text as before

<a id="setting-help.operation-max"></a>
### `help.operation-max`

integer · default `32` · section Help · declared by ochazuke

The ? help's operation and arguments columns (and the table view's mode columns) grow to their longest entry up to this many cells and wrap beyond it; 0 restores the fixed 18-cell operation column (arguments 22, modes 24)

<a id="setting-help.pending-modes"></a>
### `help.pending-modes`

boolean · default `false` · section Help · declared by ochazuke

The ? help's pick and table views offer the pending modes too (counts, operators, the terminal leader, key-sequence prefixes)

<a id="setting-help.pick-view"></a>
### `help.pick-view`

boolean · default `true` · section Help · declared by ochazuke

S in the ? help shows the keys for a noun and mode you pick

<a id="setting-help.table-unbound"></a>
### `help.table-unbound`

boolean · default `true` · section Help · declared by ochazuke

The ? help's table view also lists the noun's unbound verbs (those no key runs in any column, by help.unbound-scope) as rows under an unbound heading below the keys; enter runs one, a opens its args form, b binds a key to it, and the prop filter unbound = true (z /) shows only them; off leaves the table to the bound keys

<a id="setting-help.table-view"></a>
### `help.table-view`

boolean · default `true` · section Help · declared by ochazuke

S in the ? help shows a noun's keys as a table, a column per mode

<a id="setting-help.unbound-scope"></a>
### `help.unbound-scope`

string · default `focus` · choices `focus`, `chain`, `all` · section Help · declared by ochazuke

Whose unbound verbs the ? help lists: focus (the focused thing's noun), chain (every application noun from the focus out to its page) or all (also the framework's own verbs, such as list and input)

<a id="setting-help.unbound-verbs"></a>
### `help.unbound-verbs`

boolean · default `true` · section Help · declared by ochazuke

The ? help also lists the verbs the focused thing's noun has that no key runs, in a section after its keys with the key column blank; enter runs one (asking first where its key would), b binds a key to it in your bindings.json

<a id="setting-text-view.result-title"></a>
### `text-view.result-title`

boolean · default `true` · section Help · declared by ochazuke

Use a text answer's returned title; off titles it with the operation name

<a id="setting-text-view.wrap"></a>
### `text-view.wrap`

boolean · default `true` · section Help · declared by ochazuke

Soft-wrap text answers; off keeps horizontal motion and marks clipped lines with ›

## Hooks

<a id="setting-hooks.enabled"></a>
### `hooks.enabled`

boolean · default `true` · section Hooks · declared by ochazuke

Run the hook rows: the application's hooks.json (in its own config directory) and the defaults it and its extensions declare, which run a verb when an event happens (a modal, form or page closed after a change, the application quitting); off, events still happen and nothing runs

## Keys

<a id="setting-aliases.shadow"></a>
### `aliases.shadow`

string · default `refuse` · choices `refuse`, `allow` · section Keys · declared by ochazuke

A bare actions.json alias (w!, q) named like a verb: refuse skips the row and reports it; allow loads it, and typed alone it runs the alias, the verb still reached as noun verb

<a id="setting-bindings.peer-notices"></a>
### `bindings.peer-notices`

string · default `user` · choices `user`, `all`, `off` · section Keys · declared by ochazuke

Missing peer binding notices: user shows user-file warnings, all also shows catalog peer warnings, off keeps both in bindings check only

<a id="setting-clipboard"></a>
### `clipboard`

string · default `yanks` · choices `none`, `yanks`, `unnamed` · section Keys · declared by ochazuke

Which yanks also go to the system clipboard (through the terminal, OSC 52): yanks copies every yank (y), not a delete; unnamed copies every yank and delete, as Vim's clipboard=unnamed; none copies only what is yanked into the clipboard register ("+y)

<a id="setting-foreground.hold"></a>
### `foreground.hold`

string · default `on-failure` · choices `off`, `on-failure` · section Keys · declared by ochazuke

Keep a failed foreground program on screen until a key is pressed; off resumes immediately

<a id="setting-inspector.enabled"></a>
### `inspector.enabled`

boolean · default `false` · section Keys · declared by ochazuke

Show the live state inspector strip below the app frame; alt+? toggles it for this session

<a id="setting-keys.echo"></a>
### `keys.echo`

string · default `off` · choices `off`, `footer`, `badge` · section Keys · declared by ochazuke

Show the last keys pressed, as a screencast does (for recordings, demos and bug reports): off, footer (the right end of the footer line) or badge (on the title row, left of the mode badge); counts and sequences group as typed (5j, g g), text typed into an input collapses, a secret input shows nothing

<a id="setting-keys.echo-commands"></a>
### `keys.echo-commands`

boolean · default `true` · section Keys · declared by ochazuke

The key echo shows a palette line as the command it ran (:page open docs); off shows :… in its place

<a id="setting-keys.echo-count"></a>
### `keys.echo-count`

integer · default `5` · section Keys · declared by ochazuke

How many entries the key echo keeps (a key, a sequence, a run of typed text, a command)

<a id="setting-keys.echo-linger"></a>
### `keys.echo-linger`

duration · default `3s` · section Keys · declared by ochazuke

How long an entry stays in the key echo after its last key; 0s keeps it until newer ones push it out

<a id="setting-keys.echo-terminal"></a>
### `keys.echo-terminal`

boolean · default `false` · section Keys · declared by ochazuke

The key echo also shows the keys an attached terminal pane receives (its typed text collapsed); off shows only the keys ochazuke handles there (the leader and what follows it), so a password typed into a shell never shows

<a id="setting-keys.echo-typing"></a>
### `keys.echo-typing`

string · default `text` · choices `text`, `count` · section Keys · declared by ochazuke

Text typed into an input in the key echo: text shows it ("hello"), count only how many keys (typed 5); a secret input shows nothing either way

<a id="setting-keys.echo-width"></a>
### `keys.echo-width`

integer · default `28` · section Keys · declared by ochazuke

The cells the key echo reserves (at most half the line), drawn or not, so the line never reflows as keys come and go; older keys are dropped with … to fit

<a id="setting-keys.table-results"></a>
### `keys.table-results`

boolean · default `true` · section Keys · declared by ochazuke

Open a declared rows answer (result "rows") of an application verb run from a key in the results table; off leaves key results unpresented

<a id="setting-keys.text-results"></a>
### `keys.text-results`

boolean · default `true` · section Keys · declared by ochazuke

Open declared text, Markdown and preformatted answers from key bindings in their viewer; off leaves key results unpresented

<a id="setting-leader.fall-through"></a>
### `leader.fall-through`

string · default `no-motions` · choices `no-motions`, `all`, `off` · section Keys · declared by ochazuke

Offer unbound leader keys to single-key outside bindings: no-motions excludes motions and focus-bound editing; all includes them; off sends unknown sequences as before

<a id="setting-nouns.display"></a>
### `nouns.display`

string · default `shortest` · choices `shortest`, `framework`, `canonical` · section Keys · declared by ochazuke

The name hints, the ? help, the palette and the jobs ticker draw a noun by: shortest is its shortest live alias (doc for an extension's json.doc a host aliased doc; list for ochazuke.collection), never a deprecated one; framework only shortens the framework's own nouns (ochazuke.collection as list), as before; canonical draws every noun by its registered name. Output (history, bindings list, the catalog) is always canonical

<a id="setting-repeat.empty"></a>
### `repeat.empty`

string · default `info` · choices `info`, `silent` · section Keys · declared by ochazuke

Dot-repeat (.) with nothing to repeat here: info says nothing to repeat on the status line, plain; silent shows nothing

<a id="setting-results.show-data"></a>
### `results.show-data`

boolean · default `true` · section Keys · declared by ochazuke

A data answer (not text) of a verb run from the ? help or the palette is shown, one line in the status line or longer in the text view; off leaves it unshown

<a id="setting-sequence-inherit"></a>
### `sequence-inherit`

string · default `drop` · choices `drop`, `keep` · section Keys · declared by ochazuke

A key sequence a mode inherits from the mode it extends (a row's normal d d in visual-line) when the mode binds the keys typed on its own (visual-line d): drop runs the mode's own key at once, as in Vim (V j d); keep waits for the inherited sequence

<a id="setting-sequence-timeout"></a>
### `sequence-timeout`

duration · default `0s` · section Keys · declared by ochazuke

How long a pending key sequence (g g, z R, the terminal leader) waits for its next key before the shorter binding runs; 0 waits until a key comes

<a id="setting-sequence-unknown"></a>
### `sequence-unknown`

string · default `pass` · choices `pass`, `swallow` · section Keys · declared by ochazuke

A key no binding continues a pending sequence with: pass ends the sequence (its shorter binding runs) and handles the key as if typed alone; swallow drops the sequence and the key with a notice

<a id="setting-subject.from-association"></a>
### `subject.from-association`

boolean · default `true` · section Keys · declared by ochazuke

Let declared human requests act through reference props marked association on the focused thing; off uses only ordinary noun ancestry

<a id="setting-yank.report"></a>
### `yank.report`

boolean · default `true` · section Keys · declared by ochazuke

A yank in an editor or the read-only text view says on the status line what it copied (copied 1 line, copied 12 characters), as a table's y does; off yanks silently. Vim reports only past 'report' lines

## Lists

<a id="setting-collection.archived-count"></a>
### `collection.archived-count`

boolean · default `true` · section Lists · declared by ochazuke

Say on a list's filter line how many archived rows it hides (3 archived hidden; z a shows them); off says nothing

<a id="setting-collection.group-by"></a>
### `collection.group-by`

string · default `""` · section Lists · declared by ochazuke

Props to group the rows of a list by, comma-separated (the first row of each group carries its heading); a list whose rows lack one of the props is not grouped; empty groups nothing, as before. The collection.group verb sets one list's own grouping

<a id="setting-collection.hide-archived"></a>
### `collection.hide-archived`

boolean · default `true` · section Lists · declared by ochazuke

Hide things with their archive-role prop set in standard list results and in row-fed lists, trees and pages, unless where or a filter (the saved archived filter) names that prop; off includes archived things

<a id="setting-collection.no-spill"></a>
### `collection.no-spill`

list · default `[]` · section Lists · declared by ochazuke

Instance ids of lists, tables, trees and timelines whose motions stay inside them at the edges instead of moving the focus to the next or previous stop, as a list made with NoSpill does; a tree or timeline is named by its own id (panes/working), an entry ending in * is a prefix (panes/*); a suffix names one edge: :last (j past the last row), :first (k before the first), :last-col and :first-col (a table's l and h at its column edge; a no-op where nothing moves sideways), no suffix all four (panes/working:last); at a trapped edge the motion is unavailable and the key goes on to the next row bound to it; empty, every list on a page spills

<a id="setting-collection.per-page"></a>
### `collection.per-page`

integer · default `0` · section Lists · declared by ochazuke

Rows per page in lists the widget draws (a page counts rows, never groups; the list indicator shows the page and collection.page-next and collection.page-prev move it); 0 shows every row on one page, as before. The CLI's list verb pages only when asked (--per-page)

<a id="setting-collection.sort-indicator"></a>
### `collection.sort-indicator`

boolean · default `true` · section Lists · declared by ochazuke

Show sort arrows in column titles and the form, or a separate sort label in plain lists and pickers; later keys include their priority (▲2, ▼2). Off keeps sorting and hides the indicators

<a id="setting-collection.sort-sections"></a>
### `collection.sort-sections`

string · default `within` · choices `within`, `off` · section Lists · declared by ochazuke

Sort rows within each contiguous section, retaining section order; off does not offer local sorting on sectioned lists

<a id="setting-collection.window"></a>
### `collection.window`

integer · default `200` · section Lists · declared by ochazuke

Rows a list fed by a store that pages (Store.Query) reads at a time: the list holds one page of the store, its filters, sort and archive toggle go into the query, and the page keys read the next page; 0 reads the whole store

<a id="setting-rename.select"></a>
### `rename.select`

boolean · default `true` · section Lists · declared by ochazuke

A rename opens with the whole name selected: typing replaces it, a motion keeps it and moves; off opens it with the cursor at the end

<a id="setting-table.fit-follows-cursor"></a>
### `table.fit-follows-cursor`

boolean · default `false` · section Lists · declared by ochazuke

A cell-mode table lays its current column out at its widest cell or title as the cursor reaches it (as Vim's winwidth widens the current window), the column going back to its width when the cursor leaves; a width given with z f, z F, z > or z < wins; off, the columns change width only on z f, z F, z >, z < and z =

<a id="setting-tree.breadcrumb"></a>
### `tree.breadcrumb`

string · default `line` · choices `line`, `title`, `off` · section Lists · declared by ochazuke

Where a zoomed tree shows the levels it hides: line (a dimmed line above its rows), title (in the header beside the mode, while the tree has the focus) or off

<a id="setting-tree.breadcrumb.ancestors"></a>
### `tree.breadcrumb.ancestors`

integer · default `2` · section Lists · declared by ochazuke

How many of the nearest hidden ancestors a zoomed tree's breadcrumb names; farther ones fold into …; 0 names them all

<a id="setting-tree.delete-children"></a>
### `tree.delete-children`

string · default `promote` · choices `promote`, `orphan`, `subtree` · section Lists · declared by ochazuke

What deleting an outline row (d d) does with its children: promote (a collapsed row deletes its subtree; an expanded row deletes only itself and its children move up one level into its place, in order), orphan (the same, but an expanded row's children move to the top level, after the row's top-level ancestor) or subtree (always the row and everything under it). u restores the exact structure either way. A fixed row still refuses

<a id="setting-tree.guides"></a>
### `tree.guides`

string · default `app` · choices `app`, `off` · section Lists · declared by ochazuke

Tree branch lines: app keeps each tree's Guides choice (default off); off hides guides everywhere

<a id="setting-tree.remove-empty-rows"></a>
### `tree.remove-empty-rows`

boolean · default `true` · section Lists · declared by ochazuke

Leaving an outline row's line with no text removes the row: a new row left blank, or a row edited down to nothing. The removal is one undo step with the edit that emptied the row and the cursor lands on the row it was added from, else the next row. A row with children, a fixed row and a row that was already blank before you touched it stay. Off keeps empty rows

<a id="setting-tree.space-above"></a>
### `tree.space-above`

boolean · default `true` · section Lists · declared by ochazuke

Draw the blank line a tree asks for above some rows (an application marks them, such as the project rows of an outline), never above the first row shown. The blank line is not a row: motions, selection and scrolling count rows only. Off draws the rows with no gaps

<a id="setting-tree.spill"></a>
### `tree.spill`

string · default `left` · choices `left`, `both`, `off` · section Lists · declared by ochazuke

Which of a tree's h/l act as on a table where the tree has nothing to do on the row: left (h on a closed or childless top-level node scrolls the columns back, then moves the focus to the previous stop), both (l on a leaf also scrolls, then moves to the next stop) or off (neither)

<a id="setting-tree.zoom"></a>
### `tree.zoom`

string · default `manual` · choices `manual`, `auto`, `off` · section Lists · declared by ochazuke

Tree zoom: manual (only z +, z -, z 0 and h past the top), auto (also zooms when the selected row's indent takes over half the tree's width) or off (no zoom)

<a id="setting-tree.zoom.root"></a>
### `tree.zoom.root`

string · default `crumb` · choices `crumb`, `row` · section Lists · declared by ochazuke

Where a tree's zoomed-on node goes: crumb (it ends the breadcrumb and its children are the top rows) or row (it stays as the top row)

<a id="setting-visual.after-action"></a>
### `visual.after-action`

string · default `end` · choices `end`, `keep` · section Lists · declared by ochazuke

After a key acts on a visual selection of list rows (V j d): end leaves the selection and visual-line, as in Vim; keep keeps the selection on the rows still shown, so the next key acts on them too

<a id="setting-visual.list"></a>
### `visual.list`

string · default `mode` · choices `mode`, `marks` · section Lists · declared by ochazuke

V on a list, table or tree: mode enters visual-line, where single keys act on the selection (d, y, an application's own); marks selects in normal mode, as before, the rows' normal keys acting on the selection

## Markdown

<a id="setting-markdown.cursor"></a>
### `markdown.cursor`

string · default `item` · choices `item`, `line` · section Markdown · declared by ochazuke

Markdown cursor unit: whole elements, or individual drawn lines

<a id="setting-markdown.cursor-width"></a>
### `markdown.cursor-width`

string · default `pane` · choices `pane`, `text` · section Markdown · declared by ochazuke

Markdown cursor highlight width: the whole pane, or only its text

<a id="setting-markdown.done"></a>
### `markdown.done`

string · default `show` · choices `show`, `hide` · section Markdown · declared by ochazuke

Show checked Markdown tasks, or hide them with their nested subtrees

<a id="setting-markdown.done-indicator"></a>
### `markdown.done-indicator`

boolean · default `true` · section Markdown · declared by ochazuke

Show a dim count above a Markdown document when checked tasks are hidden

<a id="setting-markdown.extra-space"></a>
### `markdown.extra-space`

boolean · default `false` · section Markdown · declared by ochazuke

Add one blank line between rendered Markdown components, including adjacent list items

<a id="setting-markdown.link-stops"></a>
### `markdown.link-stops`

boolean · default `true` · section Markdown · declared by ochazuke

Visit inline Markdown links as focus stops with j and k

<a id="setting-markdown.link-urls"></a>
### `markdown.link-urls`

string · default `focused` · choices `focused`, `always`, `never` · section Markdown · declared by ochazuke

When a Markdown link's URL is drawn after its text: focused shows only the focused link's URL, on a line under the document; always draws every URL; never draws none. Opening and copying a link use its URL either way

<a id="setting-markdown.note-author"></a>
### `markdown.note-author`

string · default `owner` · section Markdown · declared by ochazuke

The author a new note in a Markdown document is signed with

<a id="setting-markdown.wrap"></a>
### `markdown.wrap`

boolean · default `true` · section Markdown · declared by ochazuke

Soft-wrap long lines in the Markdown block editor at the last space that fits; off, they scroll sideways. The source never gets added line breaks

## Modals

<a id="setting-modal.esc-closes"></a>
### `modal.esc-closes`

boolean · default `false` · section Modals · declared by ochazuke

esc closes a modal as it did before (a modal text input stays in insert); off, esc only leaves insert for the modal's normal mode (it does nothing in normal mode) and q closes the modal

## Open

<a id="setting-open.modal"></a>
### `open.modal`

boolean · default `true` · section Open · declared by ochazuke

The open modal (ochazuke.opener.show, no default key): an input that takes a link, a path, a file or a noun:id and shows what open would do. Off, opener.show refuses and opener.run still opens

<a id="setting-open.openers"></a>
### `open.openers`

string · default `[]` · section Open · declared by ochazuke

Your opener rows, tried before the built-in ones, as a JSON array: each has one of scheme (http), prefix (~/), ext (png) or noun (a noun name, or * for any) and an action (os-open, os-reveal, page, viewer, verb) with to (the page, noun.verb, or the verbs to try on a noun:id)

<a id="setting-open.unmatched"></a>
### `open.unmatched`

string · default `os` · choices `os`, `none` · section Open · declared by ochazuke

Text no opener row matches: os hands it to the OS opener (a typo opens nothing visible, never a refusal); none does nothing

<a id="setting-paths.free-verbs"></a>
### `paths.free-verbs`

boolean · default `true` · section Open · declared by ochazuke

A noun with a prop of Type path gets the free verbs reveal, yank-path, open and open-with. Off, they refuse to run and the noun has only the verbs it declares

## Pages

<a id="setting-anyref.nouns"></a>
### `anyref.nouns`

string · default `stored` · choices `stored`, `pickers` · section Pages · declared by ochazuke

Nouns the chooser of an any-noun reference (a note's about) offers: stored lists the application's nouns that have a store (not the framework's own views); pickers lists every noun with a picker, the framework's own views included

<a id="setting-detail.padding"></a>
### `detail.padding`

integer · default `1` · section Pages · declared by ochazuke

Whitespace around catalog main sections: one blank line and two inset cells per unit; also separates thread headers from indented bodies. 0 restores the tight layout; page padding overrides

<a id="setting-detail.related"></a>
### `detail.related`

boolean · default `true` · section Pages · declared by ochazuke

Show the things that name the selected row (its notes, tasks, tags: one section per noun that references its noun) as sections in a page's detail; off leaves the detail as it was

<a id="setting-detail.related-hidden"></a>
### `detail.related-hidden`

list · default `[]` · section Pages · declared by ochazuke

Related sections kept out of details, as NOUN.PROP ids (note.about hides notes everywhere; a trailing * is a prefix)

<a id="setting-detail.sections"></a>
### `detail.sections`

boolean · default `true` · section Pages · declared by ochazuke

Render catalog section details as read-only Markdown, threads and metadata; off shows the legacy record fields

<a id="setting-detail.show-form"></a>
### `detail.show-form`

boolean · default `true` · section Pages · declared by ochazuke

Draw a noun's index page detail as the edit form over the selected thing's props: read-only until a field is edited (i), each change written as it is typed, u undoes; off shows its props as text

<a id="setting-detail.side"></a>
### `detail.side`

boolean · default `true` · section Pages · declared by ochazuke

Show side regions of catalog section details (a catalog page may override this default or name its own setting)

<a id="setting-detail.side-width"></a>
### `detail.side-width`

integer · default `96` · section Pages · declared by ochazuke

Minimum detail content width for side regions on the right; below it they follow the main content (minimum 40, page sideWidth overrides)

<a id="setting-history-fetches"></a>
### `history-fetches`

boolean · default `false` · section Pages · declared by ochazuke

Keep data requests (fetches) in the history file too

<a id="setting-history-limit"></a>
### `history-limit`

integer · default `500` · section Pages · declared by ochazuke

Action history entries kept across restarts (0 keeps none)

<a id="setting-nouns.count-lists"></a>
### `nouns.count-lists`

boolean · default `false` · section Pages · declared by ochazuke

Count a noun on the Nouns page by listing all its things when its store cannot answer one page (no Query); off shows – for its count and never reads the whole store to draw the page

<a id="setting-nouns.kinds"></a>
### `nouns.kinds`

list · default `["record","singleton","facts","instances","command"]` · section Pages · declared by ochazuke

The noun kinds the Nouns page lists, in group order: record, singleton, facts, instances, command, part (parts, drawn rows and widgets, are left out by default)

<a id="setting-nouns.page"></a>
### `nouns.page`

boolean · default `true` · section Pages · declared by ochazuke

Show the Nouns page (every noun with its kind, count, archived count and store; command nouns with their actions) as the last tab; off keeps it out of the tabs, and noun-browser.open, the page picker and the palette still open it

<a id="setting-pages.hidden"></a>
### `pages.hidden`

list · default `[]` · section Pages · declared by ochazuke

Page ids left out of the tabs and ctrl+j/k (page.hide and page.show write it); page.open still opens them

<a id="setting-pages.pinned"></a>
### `pages.pinned`

list · default `[]` · section Pages · declared by ochazuke

Opt-in pages put in the tabs, by page id: a noun's generated index page (nouns/task) is never a tab unless it is listed here

<a id="setting-relations.sections"></a>
### `relations.sections`

boolean · default `true` · section Pages · declared by ochazuke

Related sections that read relations: the things that point at the thing through a relation-backed prop or a declared relation kind, and the things it is related to. Off draws and reads none of them; the other sections are unchanged

## Palette

<a id="setting-cli.standard-verbs"></a>
### `cli.standard-verbs`

string · default `line` · choices `line`, `list` · section Palette · declared by ochazuke

How the CLI's help shows a noun's standard verbs (get, list, set, rename and the rest): line names them on one line of the noun's help (BIN NOUN --help) and after std in its summary, the noun's own verbs keeping their entries; list gives each its own entry with its parameters. Every verb runs either way

<a id="setting-cli.verb-first"></a>
### `cli.verb-first`

boolean · default `true` · section Palette · declared by ochazuke

A command word that names no command of the tool but is an action of its nouns runs that action (BIN add, BIN lane state), read as the palette reads it (both orders, the second word naming the noun, else the tool's main noun); a framework noun's short name (list) gives way when the tool's own nouns read the words; off keeps the BIN NOUN VERB spelling alone

<a id="setting-forms.single-path"></a>
### `forms.single-path`

string · default `picker` · choices `picker`, `alone`, `form` · section Palette · declared by ochazuke

A key or command line whose only missing required argument is a path: picker opens the path picker at once and its pick runs the action (optional arguments left out); alone does so only when the path is its one argument; form opens the args form (on the path, its picker open over it)

<a id="setting-lexicon.punctuation"></a>
### `lexicon.punctuation`

boolean · default `true` · section Palette · declared by ochazuke

Punctuation narrows how the leading words read, in the palette and the CLI: a.b is noun.action (json.doc.rows), a, b is action, noun (rows, json.doc), spaces allowed around the mark; off reads . and , as ordinary characters

<a id="setting-palette.active-page"></a>
### `palette.active-page`

boolean · default `true` · section Palette · declared by ochazuke

Prefer the active page's actions within the palette's existing completion groups; exact words, focus-path nouns, standard-verb groups and parameter choices keep their ordering. Off keeps the previous order

<a id="setting-palette.choice-label"></a>
### `palette.choice-label`

string · default `label-first` · choices `label-first`, `id-first` · section Palette · declared by ochazuke

How the palette's completions and a form's chips show a choice that has a label: label-first draws the label then the short id dim, as pickers do; id-first draws the id then the label (the look before this setting)

<a id="setting-palette.choice-words"></a>
### `palette.choice-words`

string · default `word` · choices `word`, `id` · section Palette · declared by ochazuke

What the palette completes and accepts for a choice that has a word of its own (a page's title for page open): word offers and takes that word (its id still runs when typed whole); id offers the ids, as before

<a id="setting-palette.marker"></a>
### `palette.marker`

string · default `line` · choices `line`, `arrow` · section Palette · declared by ochazuke

How the palette's focused completion is shown: line fills the whole row with the palette.focus tone; arrow marks it with a > before the row, as before

<a id="setting-palette.missing-opens-form"></a>
### `palette.missing-opens-form`

boolean · default `true` · section Palette · declared by ochazuke

Enter on a command line, or a key, whose action lacks a required argument opens a form for its arguments; off names the missing word instead

<a id="setting-palette.namespace-words"></a>
### `palette.namespace-words`

boolean · default `true` · section Palette · declared by ochazuke

Leading words that join with dots into a noun read as that noun, as on the CLI (json doc rows is json.doc rows), and the words after a namespace complete to its nouns (json then doc); off reads only the dotted spelling

<a id="setting-palette.noun-tails"></a>
### `palette.noun-tails`

boolean · default `true` · section Palette · declared by ochazuke

A word no noun or alias claims reads as the namespaced nouns whose last part it is: one such noun is taken (doc for json.doc), several are offered by their full names (json.doc, md.doc) and none is picked; off leaves such a word unresolved

<a id="setting-palette.pair-words"></a>
### `palette.pair-words`

boolean · default `true` · section Palette · declared by ochazuke

The palette reads the first two words as a pair in both orders (t r up is transform row, row transform as well): the readings the words fit are ranked and one is taken, several are listed as noun verb pairs; off reads only a whole first word followed by its complement

<a id="setting-palette.reach"></a>
### `palette.reach`

boolean · default `true` · section Palette · declared by ochazuke

The palette offers every action of every noun from wherever it opens, and runs the one chosen at a thing of its noun, asking (with the noun's picker) for the target nothing focused supplies, instead of leaving out a verb the focus or page does not allow; off lists only what the focus and mode allow, as before

<a id="setting-palette.standard-verbs"></a>
### `palette.standard-verbs`

list · default `["last","tag","record"]` · section Palette · declared by ochazuke

How the palette shows the standard verbs (get, list, create, set, delete, watch): one ordering, last (a noun's named verbs first), mixed (one alphabetical list) or hidden (left out of the verb list; typing the name still runs one), plus tag (a std tag beside each) and record (get shows prop and value rows); a part left out is today's palette, so [] turns them all off

<a id="setting-palette.style"></a>
### `palette.style`

string · default `classic` · choices `classic`, `board` · section Palette · declared by ochazuke

How the command palette is drawn and walked: classic is the line with its completion list beneath; board shows the first two words as a board of cells (nouns with their verb counts, then verbs with their noun counts), narrows it as you type, emphasises the shortest prefix that picks each cell, commits the one cell left, then shows only the other kind (a noun's verbs, a verb's nouns); the line, the arguments and the run are the same in both. Switches at once

<a id="setting-palette.text-results"></a>
### `palette.text-results`

string · default `editor` · choices `editor`, `all`, `plain` · section Palette · declared by ochazuke

How the palette shows a verb's text result (a verb declared TextResult, such as a jq program or a JSON mapping): editor opens it in a read-only editor (one line or many, by the text) to move, select with v, V or ctrl+v and yank with y; all does that too for any other string answer; plain shows a text result as before (a JSON array in the results table, else nothing)

## Pickers

<a id="setting-actions.focused-picker"></a>
### `actions.focused-picker`

boolean · default `true` · section Pickers · declared by ochazuke

ochazuke.focus.act (no default key) opens a picker of the verbs the focused thing has, with their keys; enter runs one on it. Off, the verb refuses

<a id="setting-path.field"></a>
### `path.field`

string · default `picker` · choices `picker`, `text` · section Pickers · declared by ochazuke

A path field in a form: picker (a stop whose enter, space or i opens the path picker) or text (typed freely; enter in normal mode or ctrl+space opens the path picker)

<a id="setting-path.find"></a>
### `path.find`

boolean · default `true` · section Pickers · declared by ochazuke

Every path picker offers the find source: every path under its folder, indexed with Git's ignore rules and fuzzy-ranked, with size, modified and a preview; off leaves it out except where asked for by name (picker.open with no name opens on it)

<a id="setting-path.first"></a>
### `path.first`

list · default `["walk"]` · section Pickers · declared by ochazuke

The path picker's sources listed first, in this order (the rest keep theirs: browse, recent, typed, then the application's); a picker opened on no source, with none remembered, opens on the first. Empty keeps the order as it was

<a id="setting-path.hidden"></a>
### `path.hidden`

boolean · default `false` · section Pickers · declared by ochazuke

The path picker's browse source lists hidden entries (names starting with .); off, typing a path starting with . still lists them

<a id="setting-path.no-auto-list"></a>
### `path.no-auto-list`

list · default `["/Volumes/","/mnt/","/media/","/run/media/"]` · section Pickers · declared by ochazuke

Folders under these prefixes (external volumes) are never listed on their own: browse waits until you open one or type a path into it

<a id="setting-path.recent-dirs"></a>
### `path.recent-dirs`

boolean · default `true` · section Pickers · declared by ochazuke

The path picker's recent source lists recent directories during file picks, opening into the directory; off lists only recent files

<a id="setting-path.start"></a>
### `path.start`

string · default `base` · choices `base`, `home`, `cwd` · section Pickers · declared by ochazuke

Where the path picker's browse starts when the parameter names no base and the field is empty: base (the folder the application gives, such as the open file's, else the working directory), home or cwd

<a id="setting-path.walk"></a>
### `path.walk`

boolean · default `true` · section Pickers · declared by ochazuke

The path picker offers the walk source when the application gives it roots (a project's folders): every folder under them (files too for a file pick), streamed in as found; off leaves it out

<a id="setting-path.walk-depth"></a>
### `path.walk-depth`

integer · default `8` · section Pickers · declared by ochazuke

How many folders deep the walk source goes below each root

<a id="setting-path.walk-hidden"></a>
### `path.walk-hidden`

boolean · default `false` · section Pickers · declared by ochazuke

The walk source lists and enters hidden folders (names starting with .); off, only the names path.walk-include gives

<a id="setting-path.walk-ignore"></a>
### `path.walk-ignore`

list · default `[".git","node_modules","vendor",".cache","target","__pycache__",".venv"]` · section Pickers · declared by ochazuke

Names (globs) the walk source never lists or enters

<a id="setting-path.walk-include"></a>
### `path.walk-include`

list · default `[".worktrees"]` · section Pickers · declared by ochazuke

Hidden names (globs) the walk source lists and enters while path.walk-hidden is off: a repo's worktrees are folders worth picking

<a id="setting-path.walk-limit"></a>
### `path.walk-limit`

integer · default `20000` · section Pickers · declared by ochazuke

The most paths the walk source lists; it stops there and its title says so

<a id="setting-picker.claim-source"></a>
### `picker.claim-source`

boolean · default `true` · section Pickers · declared by ochazuke

A picker source that recognises the query answers for it at once, whichever source is showing (a path picker: a query starting with /, ~, ./ or ../ lists path completions, enter picks); off leaves the source switch (ctrl+o) to you

<a id="setting-picker.columns"></a>
### `picker.columns`

boolean · default `true` · section Pickers · declared by ochazuke

A picker row that carries cells (a list verb's cells: status, topic, age) draws them as aligned columns; off draws the label alone

<a id="setting-picker.derive"></a>
### `picker.derive`

boolean · default `true` · section Pickers · declared by ochazuke

Every noun with a list verb gets a picker named after it (picker.open NOUN, listed by the pickers picker), unless the noun opts out or a declared picker covers it; off leaves only declared pickers

<a id="setting-picker.enter"></a>
### `picker.enter`

string · default `open` · choices `open`, `pick` · section Pickers · declared by ochazuke

Enter on a picker row that can be both opened and picked (a folder in a folder picker): open browses into it (alt+enter picks it), pick takes it (ctrl+l opens it)

<a id="setting-picker.hidden-count"></a>
### `picker.hidden-count`

boolean · default `true` · section Pickers · declared by ochazuke

Show the count of matching picker rows outside the visible window on its query line; off hides the count

<a id="setting-picker.params"></a>
### `picker.params`

boolean · default `true` · section Pickers · declared by ochazuke

A form field whose parameter names a noun (and no source of its own) opens that noun's registered picker: its rows and match mode; off opens the plain choice picker over the noun's list

<a id="setting-picker.picker-list"></a>
### `picker.picker-list`

string · default `all` · choices `all`, `declared` · section Pickers · declared by ochazuke

What the pickers picker (picker.open pickers) lists: all, the declared pickers and the derived noun pickers; declared hides the derived ones (picker.list still lists every one)

<a id="setting-picker.remember-source"></a>
### `picker.remember-source`

boolean · default `true` · section Pickers · declared by ochazuke

A picker with several sources (tab cycles them) reopens on the source last used for its kind; off opens on its first source

<a id="setting-picker.scopes"></a>
### `picker.scopes`

boolean · default `true` · section Pickers · declared by ochazuke

A picker for a parameter opens on its first scope (a declared Scope list, else all then archived for a noun that archives) and S (alt+s while typing) steps through the others, the last holding every possible value; the search line's tag names the scope and how many more the widest holds. Off opens every picker over the parameter's own choices

<a id="setting-picker.show-ids"></a>
### `picker.show-ids`

boolean · default `true` · section Pickers · declared by ochazuke

A picker row for a thing with a label draws the thing's short id dim after the label (Choice.Row); off hides the id, and the filter still matches it

<a id="setting-picker.stable-height"></a>
### `picker.stable-height`

boolean · default `true` · section Pickers · declared by ochazuke

A picker keeps the height it reached while it is open: as typing narrows the matches, blank rows hold its size so the search line does not move (R4.9); off sizes it to the rows that match

<a id="setting-pickers.directory.section-limit"></a>
### `pickers.directory.section-limit`

integer · default `5` · section Pickers · declared by ochazuke

The most rows a section of the hybrid path picker shows while the search line is empty; typing shows every row that matches

<a id="setting-pickers.directory.style"></a>
### `pickers.directory.style`

string · default `list` · choices `list`, `hybrid`, `columns` · section Pickers · declared by ochazuke

How every path picker (a project directory, a pin, a move, a form's path field, a mounted extension's path parameter) is drawn: list (the sources one at a time, ctrl+o between them; the picker as it always was), hybrid (Recent, the application's sections and Browse on show together; ] and [ jump between sections; esc leaves the search line for the browse keys) or columns (the folder above, the folder and a preview of the highlighted entry side by side; h and l move between columns). Every style goes up to / from wherever it starts and takes any typed or pasted path; switching is live

## Records

<a id="setting-copies.delete"></a>
### `copies.delete`

string · default `local` · choices `local`, `source` · section Records · declared by ochazuke

What the standard delete of a copied thing (a noun whose store is a copy of a source) does: local deletes the copy alone and keeps a tombstone, so the next list does not copy it in again; source deletes it at the source too

<a id="setting-copies.marks"></a>
### `copies.marks`

boolean · default `true` · section Records · declared by ochazuke

A list row of a copied thing ends with ≠ while its copy differs from what the last refresh read at the source and no pick kept the copy's value; off shows no mark (differences never block anything either way)

<a id="setting-create.from-focus"></a>
### `create.from-focus`

boolean · default `true` · section Records · declared by ochazuke

A standard create fills a reference prop declared fromFocus (a new task's project) from the focused thing of its noun when you leave it out, and says so: the palette slot, the args form and a notice show the value; off fills nothing and the reference stays empty

<a id="setting-delete.archive"></a>
### `delete.archive`

boolean · default `false` · section Records · declared by ochazuke

A standard delete on a noun with an archive prop archives a live thing (sets the prop) and deletes an archived one for real; the confirm says which (delete.archive-confirm); off, delete is the store's delete; nouns without an archive prop are unchanged

<a id="setting-delete.archive-confirm"></a>
### `delete.archive-confirm`

boolean · default `true` · section Records · declared by ochazuke

With delete.archive on, a delete that will only archive the thing asks first, saying so (Archive task X? delete it again to delete it for good); off archives without asking (restore undoes it); the real delete of an archived thing always asks

<a id="setting-edit.field-only"></a>
### `edit.field-only`

boolean · default `true` · section Records · declared by ochazuke

edit with a field (edit {field: "@label"}, the r and m keys) opens a form holding only that field, its value selected as a rename's (rename.select); off opens the full form with that field focused

<a id="setting-edit.field-picker"></a>
### `edit.field-picker`

boolean · default `true` · section Records · declared by ochazuke

edit with a field that takes a choice (an enum, a choice source, a noun reference, a boolean) opens that field's picker in place of the one-field form: the pick writes (one undo step) and closes it, esc writes nothing; off (or edit.field-only off) opens the form. A key row's picker argument (edit {field, picker: false}) overrides it

<a id="setting-forms.dependent-choices"></a>
### `forms.dependent-choices`

boolean · default `true` · section Records · declared by ochazuke

Refresh dependent field choices when sibling values change, retaining all values and marking free values outside the current choices; off refreshes choices only when their picker opens

<a id="setting-forms.edit"></a>
### `forms.edit`

boolean · default `true` · section Records · declared by ochazuke

Generate edit on nouns with readable stores and writable declared props, including catalog mounts; set before declaring stores or mounting catalogs. An application's own edit is unchanged

<a id="setting-forms.edit-apply"></a>
### `forms.edit-apply`

string · default `change` · choices `change`, `confirm` · section Records · declared by ochazuke

Apply implicit noun edits on change: typing debounced, field leave, close and quit flushed, with undo instead of discard. Confirm waits for Enter and Escape cancels. Read when the form opens

<a id="setting-forms.inverted-tone"></a>
### `forms.inverted-tone`

boolean · default `true` · section Records · declared by ochazuke

Draw inverted record fields (not) in the record.inverted theme tone, including their labels and values; off keeps their usual colours

<a id="setting-forms.outside-write"></a>
### `forms.outside-write`

string · default `reload` · choices `reload`, `close` · section Records · declared by ochazuke

A record editor open on a record that is written from outside it (a set from the palette, another client): reload takes the new values and stays open, keeping the focus, the field and the mode (a field with unsaved typing keeps the typing); close leaves the editor

<a id="setting-forms.show-read-only"></a>
### `forms.show-read-only`

boolean · default `true` · section Records · declared by ochazuke

The standard edit form (the edit verb's modal and a form placed with Runtime.EditSpec) also draws the thing's read-only props, muted and with no focus stop; off draws only what can be edited. Read when the form opens

<a id="setting-input.newlines-grow"></a>
### `input.newlines-grow`

boolean · default `true` · section Records · declared by ochazuke

Text with line breaks (a paste, a register put, a set) makes a single-line input multi-line in place and is kept as it is; off turns each line break into a space. An input never refuses text either way

## Search

<a id="setting-collection.filter-chip-max"></a>
### `collection.filter-chip-max`

integer · default `24` · section Search · declared by ochazuke

In collection.filter-layout=fields, a field with more values than this completes typed values instead of showing chips; compact always uses a value picker

<a id="setting-collection.filter-clear-hidden-sort"></a>
### `collection.filter-clear-hidden-sort`

boolean · default `false` · section Search · declared by ochazuke

Clear the view sort with form.clear even when sort controls are hidden; off preserves a sort the form does not show

<a id="setting-collection.filter-cycle"></a>
### `collection.filter-cycle`

boolean · default `true` · section Search · declared by ochazuke

Enable cycling saved prop filters in lists, trees and pickers

<a id="setting-collection.filter-form"></a>
### `collection.filter-form`

boolean · default `true` · section Search · declared by ochazuke

The prop filter key (ochazuke.collection.filter-prop with no prop) opens the filter form over the list, tree or picker: compact field and value pickers with active conditions, is/not and live updates; collection.filter-layout=fields retains a field per prop. Off opens the prop picker, then the value picker, as before

<a id="setting-collection.filter-keeps-children"></a>
### `collection.filter-keeps-children`

boolean · default `true` · section Search · declared by ochazuke

The / filter keeps a matching row's child rows (ListItem.Under) and a matching child's parent row

<a id="setting-collection.filter-layout"></a>
### `collection.filter-layout`

string · default `compact` · choices `compact`, `fields` · section Search · declared by ochazuke

Filter modal layout: compact searches one prop and its values with active condition rows; fields keeps the original field-per-prop form

<a id="setting-collection.filter-linger"></a>
### `collection.filter-linger`

duration · default `30s` · section Search · declared by ochazuke

Keep changed rows that leave an active filter visible with a ~ marker and the list.lingering tone for this long; 0 disables. Changing the filter or collection.flush-lingering removes them at once

<a id="setting-collection.filter-picker-sort"></a>
### `collection.filter-picker-sort`

boolean · default `false` · section Search · declared by ochazuke

Offer the shared Sort action in the older prop picker when rows allow local sorting; off keeps the original prop-only picker

<a id="setting-collection.filter-save"></a>
### `collection.filter-save`

boolean · default `true` · section Search · declared by ochazuke

Show the name input for saving or replacing conditions and sort in collection.filters from the filter form

<a id="setting-collection.filter-sort"></a>
### `collection.filter-sort`

boolean · default `true` · section Search · declared by ochazuke

Show the sort field and direction at the top of the filter form; off hides these controls without changing the current sort

<a id="setting-collection.filter-strip"></a>
### `collection.filter-strip`

boolean · default `true` · section Search · declared by ochazuke

Show active prop filters in the list, tree or picker header strip

<a id="setting-collection.filters"></a>
### `collection.filters`

string · default `[]` · section Search · declared by ochazuke

Saved prop filters as a JSON array: name, noun or list, where (equality props), conditions (prop/op/value) and optional sort (field/desc); user rows replace app defaults by name and scope

<a id="setting-collection.props-off"></a>
### `collection.props-off`

list · default `[]` · section Search · declared by ochazuke

Row fields prop filters never offer, as NOUN.FIELD patterns (path.Match: lane.notes, *.uuid, o-lane.lane.*); every other field of a list's rows is filterable, declared or not, and Secret props never are

<a id="setting-picker.match"></a>
### `picker.match`

string · default `fuzzy` · choices `substring`, `fuzzy`, `regex` · section Search · declared by ochazuke

How pickers, the path finder among them, match their query (substring, fuzzy or regex, as search.match); tab or ctrl+t in a picker (ctrl+t in the path finder, where tab completes; search.cycle-match) step an open one through them for that search only. A picker whose application filters or ranks its rows itself keeps its own matching

<a id="setting-picker.prop-filters"></a>
### `picker.prop-filters`

boolean · default `true` · section Search · declared by ochazuke

Enable typed prop filters and saved-filter keys in pickers with declared row props

<a id="setting-picker.up-from-none"></a>
### `picker.up-from-none`

string · default `last` · choices `last`, `stay` · section Search · declared by ochazuke

Up from no highlighted row in pickers, inline completion and palette completion: last selects the final row; stay keeps no selection. Down selects the first row

<a id="setting-search.case"></a>
### `search.case`

string · default `smart` · choices `smart`, `ignore`, `sensitive` · section Search · declared by ochazuke

How every search and filter (pickers, the path finder, the path picker's typed completion, the / list filter, the / find in text viewers and timelines) treats case: smart ignores it unless the query holds an upper-case letter, then matches it exactly (Vim's ignorecase with smartcase); ignore always ignores it; sensitive always matches it

<a id="setting-search.match"></a>
### `search.match`

string · default `substring` · choices `substring`, `fuzzy`, `regex` · section Search · declared by ochazuke

How the / list filter (lists, tables, trees) and the / find line (text view, docs viewer, Markdown viewer, timeline) match their query: substring keeps the rows holding every word of it; fuzzy the rows holding its characters in order; regex the rows a Go RE2 regular expression matches (an invalid one matches nothing and the filter line says why). tab (search.cycle-match) steps an open filter or find line through them for that search only

<a id="setting-search.open-folds"></a>
### `search.open-folds`

boolean · default `true` · section Search · declared by ochazuke

A find (/, n, N) that lands on a closed timeline card by its body opens the card, so the match shows (Vim's foldopen with search); off selects the card and leaves it closed

<a id="setting-search.show-match"></a>
### `search.show-match`

boolean · default `true` · section Search · declared by ochazuke

Show the match mode (substr, fuzzy, regex) at the right end of the / filter line, a picker's search line and the path picker's path line; off hides the tag (the mode still applies)

## Settings

<a id="setting-settings.all-section"></a>
### `settings.all-section`

boolean · default `true` · section Settings · declared by ochazuke

The Settings page lists an All section first (an All tab with settings.layout tabs): every setting in one list, each under its tab and section, edited in place; a / search in the section list lands on it, so every match from every section shows at once; A (setting.all) shows it. Off, there is no All section and a search shows the shown section's matches

<a id="setting-settings.autosave"></a>
### `settings.autosave`

boolean · default `false` · section Settings · declared by ochazuke

A session write (a :set line, setting verbs with session scope) goes straight to settings.json; off keeps it for this session until setting.write-all (alias save, mksettings). The Settings page and settings set always save at once

<a id="setting-settings.layout"></a>
### `settings.layout`

string · default `tabs+sections` · choices `tabs+sections`, `tabs`, `sections` · section Settings · declared by ochazuke

How the Settings page lays out its settings: tabs+sections (a tab per owner: the application, its extensions, ochazuke; the shown tab's sections in a list on the left), tabs (a tab per section and no section list, the page before owners) or sections (no tabs; the section list holds every owner's sections under a heading per owner)

<a id="setting-settings.mark-session"></a>
### `settings.mark-session`

boolean · default `true` · section Settings · declared by ochazuke

The Settings page draws a session value bold with the saved value beside it, stack  (saved: tabs), while the two differ

<a id="setting-settings.narrow-width"></a>
### `settings.narrow-width`

integer · default `72` · section Settings · declared by ochazuke

Below this many columns the Settings page folds its section list into a selector line at the top of the settings (h/l step it, s picks one); 0 never folds

<a id="setting-settings.search-values"></a>
### `settings.search-values`

boolean · default `true` · section Settings · declared by ochazuke

The Settings page's / filters search every setting: a section matches by its settings' names, descriptions, values, defaults and choices, the section list's filter spans every tab, and the settings pane shows the shown section's matches; off, a section matches by its title alone

## Status bar

<a id="setting-messages.hint"></a>
### `messages.hint`

boolean · default `true` · section Status bar · declared by ochazuke

Show the message.show binding beside a cut status or error; off hides the recovery hint

<a id="setting-quit.force-after"></a>
### `quit.force-after`

duration · default `500ms` · section Status bar · declared by ochazuke

Minimum time after the first quit before a second press forces exit; 0s accepts any second press. Explicit app.quit --force always leaves immediately

<a id="setting-quit.write-wait"></a>
### `quit.write-wait`

duration · default `10s` · section Status bar · declared by ochazuke

Maximum quit wait for queued writes; 0 leaves immediately. A deliberate second quit leaves and unfinished values are reported in notices and on stderr

<a id="setting-status.segment-backoff"></a>
### `status.segment-backoff`

boolean · default `true` · section Status bar · declared by ochazuke

Slow a status segment down while its answer stays the same (its refresh interval doubles up to the row's max-every, 60s by default) and reset it on a change; off refreshes every segment at its every, always

<a id="setting-status.segment-order"></a>
### `status.segment-order`

list · default `[]` · section Status bar · declared by ochazuke

Segment ids in the order the header rule draws them (segment.move writes it); the rest follow

<a id="setting-status.segments"></a>
### `status.segments`

boolean · default `true` · section Status bar · declared by ochazuke

Show the status segments (cpu, disk, an extension's) in the header rule; off hides them all and stops their refreshes
